# gop: who can make code run where in a GitHub Enterprise

Site: https://peleduri.github.io/gop/
Source: https://github.com/peleduri/gop (Apache-2.0)
MCP Registry: io.github.peleduri/gop

## What gop is

gop (GitHub Enterprise Org Posture) is an open-source, read-only tool for
security engineers. It reads a whole GitHub Enterprise with a read-only token
and writes one evidence graph, graph.json. From that graph it answers, in an
HTML report, on the command line, or to an AI assistant over the Model Context
Protocol (MCP):

- Who can make code run in this repo, workflow, Action, secret, OIDC cloud
  trust or self-hosted runner pool, and through which hops?
- What can this person, team, app or org's members make code run in, across
  every org?
- Which AI coding agents in GitHub Actions can people without push access
  start (for example with an issue comment), and what token, secrets and tools
  do they run with?
- Which Actions can members of one org push to that run in other orgs'
  workflows, including Actions nested inside composite Actions and SHA pins
  that still run a mutable ref?
- Which few changes remove the most confirmed reach: pin an action to a SHA,
  lower an org's default repository permission, restrict a workflow's
  GITHUB_TOKEN, harden a risky trigger, or remove standing org ownership?
- What could the token not see, and which access would make it visible?

gop never writes to GitHub: its API client refuses every non-GET REST request
and every GraphQL mutation before sending it. It has no telemetry and no
server; graph.json and reports stay on your disk with file mode 0600.

## Install

    go install github.com/peleduri/gop/cmd/gop@latest

Also: signed release archives for Linux, macOS and Windows
(https://github.com/peleduri/gop/releases, cosign-signed checksums, SBOMs,
SLSA provenance), the container image ghcr.io/peleduri/gop, and a GitHub
Action (peleduri/gop/action). Details:
https://github.com/peleduri/gop/blob/main/docs/install.md

## First run

Try it with no token on synthetic data:

    gop report --demo --out report.html

On your enterprise, with a read-only token (classic token of an enterprise
owner with read:enterprise, read:org and repo, or a GitHub App):

    gop doctor  --enterprise acme
    gop collect --enterprise acme --out graph.json
    gop report  --graph graph.json --out report.html

GitHub Enterprise Server works with --github-url pointing at your server.

## Use it from an AI assistant

gop serve --graph graph.json is an MCP server over stdio. Every tool is
read-only.

- Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add peleduri/gop, then
  /plugin install gop@gop (adds the MCP server and the gop skill, asks for the
  graph path). Or: claude mcp add gop -- gop serve --graph /path/to/graph.json
- Claude Desktop: open the gop_<version>_<os>_<arch>.mcpb extension from a
  release (it bundles gop and asks for graph.json).
- Cursor: the "Add gop to Cursor" install link in the README, or
  gop mcp-config --client cursor-link --graph graph.json
- Codex: codex mcp add gop -- gop serve --graph /path/to/graph.json; the skill
  installs with codex plugin marketplace add peleduri/gop and
  codex plugin add gop@gop
- VS Code: gop mcp-config --client vscode --graph graph.json
- Other MCP clients: io.github.peleduri/gop in the official MCP Registry
  (container image or .mcpb bundles)

Use an absolute graph path. graph.json is sensitive (a map of who can run code
where); keep it out of synced folders and only connect it to a model provider
your organization allows for this data. Details:
https://github.com/peleduri/gop/blob/main/docs/mcp-clients.md

## MCP tools

- who_can_reach: principals that can make code run in a target, with one
  shortest path each
- blast_radius: everything one principal can make code run in, with a score
- paths: the concrete hops from a principal, optionally to one target
- top_risks: principals ranked by confirmed blast radius
- what_if: reach before and after hypothetical fixes
- suggest_fixes: the fixes that remove the most confirmed reach
- fix_plan: concrete change steps for one fix (gop never runs them)
- explain: why one edge exists, with its evidence and API source
- coverage: what the token could not see, and the access that fixes it
- check_answerable: whether gop could see the facts an answer depends on
  (yes, partial or no); agents call it before giving a conclusion
- diff: what changed since a baseline snapshot

Resources: gop://graph/summary, gop://graph/coverage, gop://graph/schema,
gop://node/{+id}. Prompts: triage_enterprise, review_action, explain_path.

## Evidence levels

Every node and edge carries an evidence level:

- live: read from current state through the GitHub API
- inferred: derived from observed facts by a documented rule (for example
  members' push access from an org's default permission)
- audit: read from the enterprise audit log (may be stale)
- supplied: read from a file you supplied, such as a cloud OIDC trust policy
- not_visible: the token could not read it; unknown, not absent

A path whose every hop is live, inferred, recent audit or supplied is
confirmed reach. A path with any not_visible hop is possible reach: it is never
counted in headline numbers, scores or fix suggestions, and gop never reports
"could not see" as "off".
